notes: The selected analysis panel is one selection for one study design. General availability per TCGA project is reported separately and is larger; do not mix the two.
Spatial studies come from patients other than those in TCGA. They add tissue context, not measurements for TCGA patients.

Spatial resources are shown at two image levels. "Original H&E located": the original scan, measured expression and coordinates were found. "Matched data with preview image": expression and coordinates match a released preview image, and the original scan was not located; such data support molecular spatial maps, not whole-slide or tile models, cell morphology, physical distances or registration sign-off. Registration, calibration and tissue QC may be pending at either level.

Spatial section records are per study, not globally unique physical sections or independent assays. Patients are study-local IDs given by the source; sections without one add no patients, and no eligible-patient total is established.
Counts reported by a study keep that study's own unit (sections, slides, samples, donors) and are never added across studies. An unknown count is absent, not zero.
located_sections lists selection fields only; the full record with links, source wording and clinical fields is in data/captures.json under the same id.

gaps: Pei et al. primary-site sections come from rapid autopsies of end-stage disease, not early surgical resections.
HTAN pancreatic sections are labelled pancreatobiliary-type and need pathology harmonisation before pooling with conventional PDAC.
Original scans for the Schmitt et al. untreated resections have not been located.
The proposed confirmed PDAC cohort (149 patients) is one patient below the general 150-patient threshold and is shown as an explicit exception.
Eight TCGA-PAAD patients with retained assays are excluded or held because their reviewed diagnosis is adenosquamous, colloid or “Other”.
The linkage of retained assays to slide images is not yet checked for the TCGA cohort.

spatial_resources.description: Multi-cancer atlas from the Washington University HTAN centre. Breast, colorectal and pancreatic Visium captures are linked to patient-level clinical tables. Most colorectal captures are from metastases, and several breast captures were taken after neoadjuvant therapy; both groups are listed and labelled, not removed.
notes: H&E was imaged on the Visium section before library preparation (study methods). Image calibration and the full-resolution-to-spot transform have not been re-derived here.
Breast clinical annotation follows the Iglesia et al. supplement where portal coding and the clinical table disagree.
Pancreatic histology labels include pancreatobiliary-type and mixed carcinomas; these are not merged with conventional PDAC.

citation.authors: The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network

related_citations.title: An Integrated TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource to Drive High-Quality Survival Outcome Analytics

access.route: Slide images, processed RNA-seq, methylation beta values and clinical data are open on the GDC; raw sequencing reads are controlled through dbGaP. PanCanAtlas harmonized matrices and quality annotations are open downloads.

other_resources.description: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Slide images, RNA-seq and Illumina 450k methylation from the same patients, with solid normal tissue from some patients. Counts are shown after PanCanAtlas assay exclusions, after a patient-level treatment and diagnosis screen, and for the selected analysis set. Tumour slide linkage and image QC have not yet been checked beyond the histology review.
notes: Pathology-group exclusions removed neuroendocrine and acinar tumours, intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, tumours of non-pancreatic origin and samples with very low neoplastic cellularity. The retained patients are still not a curated conventional PDAC series.

A proposed confirmed PDAC cohort of 149 patients (143 with RNA-seq and 450k, six with 450k only) is defined by documented pathology review; see the PDAC page. It is one patient below the general 150-patient threshold.
Normal tissue comes from patients with cancer, usually adjacent to the tumour. It is not a healthy-donor control.
